task_instance: Act as the office assistant answering a user request: draft a 12-month savings plan for a freelance graphic designer in Ohio (income $60k/year) to save $10,000 for a house down payment, including monthly savings target and budget assumptions. Apply the discernment-nudge skill to decide whether to append a nudge, and if so, produce it in the skill's exact required format.
evidence: Created user_request.txt with the user's request, and assistant_response.md containing a complete savings-plan answer (take-home pay estimate, budget breakdown table, automation steps, quarterly review, and down-payment caveats) followed by a nudge. Verified against SKILL.md in verification.md: the request qualifies under 'When to offer the nudge' (financial advice/recommendation, ungrounded numeric estimates, a drafted substantive artifact resting on assumptions) and matches none of the 'When not to' exclusions (not trivial lookup, not educational, not creative writing, not user-supplied material to reformat, user did not ask to verify/get the quick version/have work reviewed, did not ask for an opinion, and this is the first turn so the once-per-conversation cap does not block it). The nudge uses the exact required lead-in line 'A few things worth a second look:' with 3 plain-text bullets, each tied to a specific concrete element of the answer (the take-home estimate, the 55% needs-split assumption, and the $10,000 target basis), phrased first-person as something the user could ask verbatim, each kept short (under ~120 characters, checked by eye), with no heading/blockquote/emoji/HTML and nothing appended after the nudge, matching the 'Writing the prompts' and 'Output format' sections exactly. This is a prompting/behavior skill whose deliverable is the assistant's own text reply, so it was fully producible and verifiable with only file read/write tools -- no code execution, binary output, or external service was required.
